cleared.check: L-1314. What ruint PR 603 changed, read from CHANGELOG.md and src/bits.rs at v1.18.0, v1.19.0 and v1.20.0, and whether the revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 handlers for SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE bound the count or index before calling ruint.
cleared.result: The 1.20.0 changelog lists #603 as a fix of overflow-flag false negatives in overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr, with the dependent checked, strict and saturating shifts and byte(). The bits.rs diff from 1.19.0 to 1.20.0 shows three changes. (1) overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr now OR the limbs that are shifted out entirely, and for shl the masked top bits, into the carry; the shifted value itself is unchanged. 1.18.0 and 1.19.0 both have the narrower carry. (2) The u64, u128 and u256 fast paths of wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr cast the count with rhs as u32, which in 1.19.0 turns a count of 2^32 + k into k; 1.20.0 replaces it with shift_amount, which saturates at u32::MAX. These fast paths came with #574 in 1.19.0. In 1.18.0 wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr are overflowing_shl(rhs).0 and overflowing_shr(rhs).0, which return zero once rhs / 64 >= LIMBS, so 1.18.0 has no truncating cast. (3) byte() gains a bounds assert on the big-endian path only. Both earlier readings were therefore partly right: the cast exists in 1.19.0 (MegaETH) and not in 1.18.0 (reth-bsc, X Layer, Celo reth), and the flag fix touches both. None of it reaches an EVM word. In revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 the shl and shr handlers compute shift = as_usize_saturated!(op1) and call op2 << shift or op2 >> shift only when shift < 256, else return 0; sar calls arithmetic_shr only when shift < 256, else returns all ones or 0 by the sign bit; byte calls op2.byte(31 - o1) only when o1 < 32. The handlers use the wrapping value and never the overflow flag. On the src/ side every shift count is a constant or a value below 256 (BitMath.sol:15-22 and 40-45, TickMath.sol:142-145) and every BYTE index is masked with 0x1f (BitMath.sol:21, 45), so no line of src/ can produce a count of 2^32 or more.

PR 603 (ruint 1.20.0) widens the overflow flag of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr to include limbs shifted out entirely, replaces the truncating rhs as u32 of the wrapping shift fast paths (present only since 1.19.0, #574) with a saturating cast, and adds a big-endian bounds assert to byte(). revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 call the shifts only for counts below 256 and byte() only for indices below 32 and never read the flag, so no EVM result on the ruint 1.18.0 or 1.19.0 builds can change.
